threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of just 'the train'. Locals will catch a bus or bike before they deal with that snake of a line.
Last night on the 133, a couple argued over a bagel; she swore it was 'not even toasted' while he insisted it was 'perfectly fine.' Classic Brixton drama.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I noticed the bakery on the corner started using eco-friendly bags and my neighbor's cat took up permanent residence on my balcony.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you buy fresh bread from a bakery that doubles as an art gallery, where each loaf is inspired by the latest exhibition.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they navigate BART delays; they know to carry snacks and a book instead of panicking over the schedule.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a Muni driver stop mid-route to help a lost tourist with directions. You don't see that every day in a city known for its hustle.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think all tapas are created equal, but the locals know that true patatas bravas have to burn at the edges for that perfect crunch.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell a recent arrival by their struggle with the local baker's array of pastries; they always ask for 'just a croissant,' missing out on the ensaïmadas.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still look baffled when someone asks for your ‘local’ and you realize it’s not the same. Welcome to the maze.
Last night on the N159, a guy serenaded the bus with an off-key version of 'Wonderwall' while his mates filmed it. Classic Brixton madness.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: I knew I was really here when I saw a group of kids using an old mattress as a slip 'n slide down the hill in Hasenheide. Pure Neukölln joy.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin do you find a thriving street art scene where entire buildings become canvases, then disappear overnight—artistry in a constant state of flux.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You know someone’s a local when they can name the BART delays before the alerts pop up. Can't miss that signature grumble in the queue.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a tourist hold the Muni door for a street performer mid-jam at 6th & Market. The bus driver just shook his head and kept counting to ten.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about the Gaudí architecture, but the real charm’s in the small plazas where locals gather for a simple vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They still ask for a menu in English despite being surrounded by locals chatting in Catalan at the bar. It’s a dead giveaway.
